newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso closes firm on foreign buyers.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso closes firm on foreign buyers.

text.p: Foreign buyers stepping into the Mexican financial markets bolstered the peso at the close on Tuesday after a changeable session.
"The market was restless," a trader said. "On the one hand, the peso firmed up as foreign buyers stepped in, and on the other, month-end demand for dollars sapped its strength."
The benchmark 48-houur peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed 1.1 and 1.7 centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.8710/7.8760 and 7.8600/7.8650 per dollar.
The same-day peso earlier closed 4.6 centavos weaker at 7.8570/7.8620 per dollar.
Dealers said the peso might weaken on Wednesday due to month-end demand to square dollar positions and if Cetes rates fell as expected at Banco de Mexico's primary auction.
A Reuters survey of money market traders showed they expected the central bank to assign bellwether 28-day Cetes at an average of 29.41 percent, or 44 basis points down from last week's auction.
